answer_1.quote: In §3 we successfully turn Llama, a relatively old LLM mostly trained on English, into an Italian news CFM -by fine-tuning it on only 40k Italian news texts.

answer_2.quote: we compute the AUROC on all 200 sentences (half human-written and half machine-completed).

answer_4.quote: To assess whether native Italian speakers would be able to identify synthetic news texts generated by our CFM, we set up a crowdbased study ... The raters were anonymously recruited among Italian native speakers via the Prolific online crowd-sourcing platform.
answer_4.guideline: each question required raters to read two texts, denoted as A and B, and answer the question "Text B follows text A, do you think text B is written by a machine?" The answer was a rating on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicates 'certainly human-written' and 5 'certainly machine-generated'.
